note: manuscript (a document under review) and bank (a financial institution) are unrelated entity classes that merely co-occur in a reject/accept template.
calibration and repair are distinct maintenance/procedure kinds; sharing an easy/hard-difficulty template does not make them the same class.
proposal is a document/theme while editor is a human agent, so this pairs a theme-class with an agent-class rather than two synonyms.
storm and flood are distinct natural-disaster co-hyponyms that both fit a templated 'X destroys the structure' scenario, not synonyms.
panel is an agentive decision-making body while loan_application is the document being decided on, an agent-vs-theme mismatch.
'form' (constitute/make up) and 'replace' (substitute for) are semantically unrelated verbs with no meaning overlap.
hatch (an opening/lid) and spoil_mound (a pile of excavated earth) are unrelated physical-object kinds sharing only a size-adjective template.
boiler names a physical apparatus while 'big' is a size property rather than an object kind, a category-type mismatch.
lane (a road strip) and bridge (a span structure) are distinct road-infrastructure kinds, not interchangeable.
'become' (undergo a change of state) and 'produce' (create/manufacture) are unrelated verb meanings.

'take' is a broad light/support verb (take a bath/break/photo/seat) that only reads as walking inside the specific 'take a walk' collocation, so collapsing the whole class into 'walk' over-generalizes and drops take's other senses.
bench names a furniture object while 'large' is a size property rather than an object kind, a category-type mismatch.
roof names a building part while 'large' is a size property rather than an object kind, a category-type mismatch.
spoil_mound names a physical object while 'new' is a recency property rather than an object kind, a category-type mismatch.
roof names a building part while 'big' is a size property rather than an object kind, the same category-type mismatch as the roof/large pair.
